title: Faith's role and exclusion of works sufficiently set; next: Roman school on these heads
source_text: XL. Porro his sufficienter expositum putamus quae sint fidei partes in justificatione, & quo sensu opera ab illa excludantur. Sed quoniam hic multae quaestiones motae sunt, & non parva animorum contentione agitatae inter Scholam Romanam & Scholam Reformatam, operae pretium erit breviter inquirere quid de supra expositis capitibus sentiant Scholae Romanae Theologi; ut ita facilius & clarius percipi possit quaenam proprie in quaestionem vocentur, ac quanti momenti sint quae hic agitari solent controversiae.
pass_a_gloss: Further, by these things we think sufficiently explained what faith's parts in justification are, and in what sense works are excluded from it. But since here many questions have been raised and agitated with no small contention of minds between the Roman School and the Reformed School, it will be worthwhile briefly to inquire what the theologians of the Roman School think about the heads set forth above—so that it may be more easily and clearly perceived which things are properly called into question, and of how much moment are the controversies usually agitated here.
pass_b_english: Exposition of faith's role and how works are excluded is enough for now.
Next: briefly ask what Roman-school theologians hold on these heads amid the clash.

lemmas.gloss: the Roman School and the Reformed School
